target_customer: Small businesses and traders in Nigeria that borrow in groups; later retail savers and community groups
problem: Small businesses in Africa lack collateral for loans; group liability and social pressure serve as collateral and drive repayment.
business_model: Group lending with interest income, later a licensed microfinance bank and money app for savings and investing
product_category: Group lending and community money app

founders.name: Femi Iromini
founders.background_notes: Focus on financial services at the World Bank Group per YC page.

founders.name: Adedapo Sobayo
founders.background_notes: YC page says he led technology development for one of the largest digital lending apps in Africa; employer not named.

competitors.name: FairMoney
competitors.what: Nigerian mobile lender becoming a digital microfinance bank, mostly consumer loans
competitors.traction_then: About 3.5 million registered users reported in July 2021
competitors.funding_then: $42M Series B led by Tiger Global, July 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Lending app, credit scoring and collections for informal groups in Nigeria; moderate engineering, with the CTO having led a large digital lending app.

defensibility.rationale: Group lending social collateral is copyable, though licensing became a moat after Rank acquired Zazzau Microfinance Bank in 2025.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied the group model in sources found; in November 2025 Moni rebranded to Rank and acquired AjoMoney and Zazzau MFB.

market_need_then: YC description cites over 44 million SMBs in Africa; company reported $72k MRR growing 50% MoM, over $5M disbursed and 99% repayment on 11,000 loans in its YC profile (company claims).

branding.name_origin: No source explains the word Rank; coverage links the new name to bigger ambition beyond Moni's limits (CEO quote reported by outlets).
branding.domain_note: Now uses userank.com, a prefixed domain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Community and wealth oriented, tagline The money app for communities

rebrands.why: Strategy shift from community lending to a licensed money app after acquiring AjoMoney and Zazzau MFB, per TechCabal and Techpoint coverage

brand_strength.rationale: Moni was a niche lender brand and the rename in 2025 resets recognition; no evidence of viral or community driven growth found.

pivots.to: Licensed money app for communities with savings, circles and investing (Rank)
pivots.why: Rebrand and acquisitions of AjoMoney and Zazzau Microfinance Bank per TechCabal

outcome_analysis: Moni used group liability to lend to Nigerian small businesses and claimed fast growth with high repayment around the YC batch. By November 2025 it rebranded as Rank and bought AjoMoney and a microfinance bank to gain a license and expand into savings. The record shows an active company that moved from lending to broader banking, with funding totals poorly documented in primary sources.
notes: Seedtable lists a pre-seed (Jan 2022) and a $3.5M seed (June 2022); WeeTracker via Seedtable says about $4M total including a $3.5M seed from YC, 186 Ventures and others. Startuplist says about $400K total. These are aggregator or single secondary sources, so the amounts are unverified and not recorded as rounds. The one recorded round has no amount and is dated to the batch year because the company YC description names these backers without dates. Mono (a different Nigerian fintech) raised $2M in 2021 and must not be confused with Moni. Carbon and Renmoney are plausible rivals but no source dated near the batch was found. Techcabal and Technext pages returned 403 and were not read.
